notes:
Batch 5 (n 1750–2099, 350 names). Things to check:
1. Keepers' 'Stonechat', 'Stonechatter' and 'Stonechick': in northern Scotland these often meant Northern Wheatear. I mapped the plain 'Stonechat' names to European Stonechat. 'Stonechick' and 'Stonechickers', and 'Stone-chat (? Wheatear)', go to family Muscicapidae. Check high-latitude stations (Unst, Orkney, Pentland Skerries).
2. Sparrows (n 1933, 1943) are genus Passer. East-coast flocks of hundreds on passage are likely Tree Sparrows.
3. 'Sepoys' and 'Seapoys' (n 1806, 1800) are mapped to Oystercatcher as phonetic 'Sea-pies'. That is a guess, so check the stations.
4. Garbles I couldn't read: 'Tahoe ieee (Black)' (2082) and 'SuiaatGans e' (2028, possibly Solan Geese). 'Sturnus merula' (2022) is probably 'Sturnus, Merula' run together. Check the scans.
5. Heading garbles: 'Srurninz' and 'Sturninæ' (starlings, by date) go to family Sturnidae. 'STrerNINzZ' (Sterninæ, mid-May arrivals) goes to genus Sterna. 'Stricipm' (Strigidæ) and 'ScoLopacip®' (Scolopacidæ) go to their families. You may want the Sturninæ entries promoted to Common Starling.
6. 'Scolopax' alone (n 1751, 14 obs) is family Scolopacidae, because the Victorian genus included snipes. In Gätke's notes it probably means Woodcock.
7. Nomenclature traps: Sylvia luscinia = Common Nightingale but philomela = Thrush Nightingale; T. musicus = Song Thrush; Sylvia hortensis = Garden Warbler; Sterna argentata = Arctic Tern; Larus affinis = a Siberian dark-backed gull (genus only); Aquila naevia = a spotted eagle (genus Clanga).
8. 'Sooty Tern(s)' (1931, 1932) went to genus Sterna. A true Sooty Tern is very unlikely; check whether 1931 is a committee heading for a real record.
9. Vernacular names with more than one meaning, left at group or family level: Sea Lark and Strand Lark; Silver Plover; Sea Coot (unknown); Sea Pheasant; Smee Ducks; Stock Duck (Mallard or Shelduck); Sea Hawk (skuas, a guess); Scotch Linnets (genus Linaria); small hawks of various colours.
10. Shearwaters are family Procellariidae, probably mostly Manx. Skuas are family Stercorariidae, probably Great Skua at Unst. Swans are genus Cygnus.
11. Editor-glossed names: Stormcocks (n 2002) are given as Fieldfare because the text says so; elsewhere Stormcock means Mistle Thrush. Sly Geese = Brent; Small Tern = S. macrura (Arctic).
12. English names follow IOC: Brant Goose (Brent in Britain), Boreal Owl (Tengmalm's), Red-throated Loon (diver), Western Barn Owl ('Screech Owl'). Shag is Gulosus aristotelis, and the whitethroats are Curruca.
